Summary:
This reference list surveys two decades of computer-vision and multimodal research illustrating how the choice, scale and construction of datasets affect model generalisation, robustness and bias. From these citations we reconstruct three intertwined causal-interventional pathways that the literature implicitly argues for: (1) scaling and diversifying datasets to mitigate dataset-induced bias, (2) removing contextual shortcuts through counterfactual data to reduce spurious correlations, and (3) crowdsourcing data across varied environments to counter demographic and environmental bias. Each pathway starts from the top-level risk of dataset-induced bias in computer-vision models and proceeds through problem analyses, theoretical insights, design rationales, implementation mechanisms and validation evidence to actionable interventions.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[80]

Inference strategy justification:
The source only provides citations without narrative text. I therefore (a) identified the key claims each cited work is known for, (b) grouped them into three coherent reasoning chains consistently discussed in the computer-vision community, and (c) inferred plausible, safety-relevant interventions supported by those works. All inference steps are marked with edge confidence ≤3.

Extraction completeness explanation:
Every distinct claim that is part of any causal chain (19 nodes total) is represented and interconnected, with no dangling nodes. Each node is named at the correct granularity to allow merging across 500 k sources (e.g. “ImageNet-scale dataset pre-training” rather than “ImageNet” or “pre-training”). Three interventions cover the major mitigation strategies implied by the references.

Key limitations:
• Lack of full paper text forced reliance on public knowledge of cited works, lowering confidence scores.  
• Validation evidence nodes summarise empirical findings broadly; finer-grained metrics are unavailable.  
• Interventions are framed at low abstraction; implementation details inside organisations may vary.
